title: NRI Voting Guide 2026: How to Register and Vote in Indian Elections From Abroad
excerpt: Indian citizens living overseas can register as voters through Form 6A, but must still travel to India to cast their ballot in person — here is everything NRIs need to know.
body:
• NRIs holding Indian citizenship can register as overseas electors using Form 6A on the Election Commission of India's Voter Portal.
  • There is currently no online, postal, or proxy voting for civilian NRIs — registered overseas electors must travel to India and vote in person at their home constituency's polling station.
  • OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) cardholders and those who have acquired foreign citizenship are not eligible to vote in Indian elections.
  • As of 2023, only about 1.15 lakh NRIs had registered as overseas voters — a fraction of the estimated 36 million Indian diaspora worldwide.

For millions of Indians living abroad, voting in Indian elections remains a civic right that is technically available but practically difficult to exercise. While the Election Commission of India (ECI) allows NRIs to register as overseas electors, the requirement to vote in person in India means only a tiny fraction actually cast ballots. With state elections ahead and the question of NRI political participation gaining attention, here is a step-by-step guide to the current process.

Who Can Register

Any Indian citizen living outside India is eligible to register as an overseas elector, provided they meet three conditions: they hold a valid Indian passport, they have not acquired citizenship of another country, and they are at least 18 years old as of January 1 of the current electoral roll revision year.

Crucially, OCI cardholders cannot vote. The overseas elector provision applies only to Indian passport holders who have not renounced their Indian citizenship.

How to Register: Form 6A

Registration is done through Form 6A — Overseas Elector Registration. Here is the process:

Step 1: Visit the ECI Citizen Service Portal at voters.eci.gov.in and create an account or sign in.

Step 2: Select "New Voter Registration (NRI)" and choose Form 6A.

Step 3: Fill in your full name, passport details, date of birth, overseas residential address, Indian address (as listed in your passport), mobile number, and email ID.

Step 4: Upload required documents — a valid Indian passport (photo page, Indian address page, and valid visa or residence permit page), a recent passport-size color photograph, and self-attested copies of all relevant pages.

Step 5: Submit the application and note your reference number for tracking.

NRIs can also submit Form 6A by post to their Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) or in person if they happen to be in India. The form is available free of cost from Indian Missions and Embassies abroad.

Verification and Approval

After submission, a Booth Level Officer (BLO) visits the Indian address listed in the applicant's passport. Family members or relatives at that address may help verify details. If local verification is not possible, documents may be verified through the concerned Indian Mission abroad. The ERO then approves or rejects the application, with decisions communicated via SMS, post, or the ECI portal.

How NRIs Actually Vote

This is where the process becomes impractical for most. Currently, a registered overseas elector must travel to India and vote in person at the designated polling station in their registered constituency. They must carry their original Indian passport for identification. No physical Voter ID card (EPIC) is issued to overseas electors.

There is no online voting, no postal ballot for civilian NRIs, and no proxy voting. The ECI has proposed introducing e-postal ballot facilities for NRIs, but the proposal has not been implemented. A 2018 bill that would have allowed proxy voting did not become law.

"The combination of cost, calendar, and visa logistics means that the conversion from 'registered NRI elector' to 'NRI elector who actually voted' is, in most elections, in the low single-digit percent."

— NRI Globe

If You Already Have an Indian Voter ID

NRIs who were previously registered as general voters in India and now wish to register as overseas electors should submit Form 6A, declare that they are not enrolled as a general elector elsewhere, and surrender their existing EPIC if one was issued.

When returning to India permanently, NRIs should inform their Electoral Registration Officer and re-register as a general elector using the applicable ECI form.

The Numbers Gap

Despite India having the world's largest diaspora at an estimated 36 million people, overseas voter registration remains negligible. As of January 2023, approximately 1.15 lakh NRIs had registered as overseas voters. The logistical barrier of in-person voting means actual turnout among registered NRI electors is in the low single digits in most elections.

Advocacy groups and NRI organizations continue to push for e-postal ballots and embassy-based voting, but legislative progress has been slow. For now, NRIs who want their vote to count must plan a trip to India around election dates — a commitment that limits participation to those with the time, resources, and flexibility to travel.

nri_angle: A practical guide for NRIs in the U.S. who want to participate in Indian elections, covering the registration process and the in-person voting requirement that limits diaspora turnout.
